title: Verifier characterization implies randomized polynomial time
statement: Let $p:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q$ and let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If there are constants $a,k\in\mathbb N$ and a polynomial-time Boolean verifier whose acceptance probability on each $x\in L$ and rejection probability on each $x\notin L$, using uniformly random bit strings of length $a(|x|+1)^k$, are each at least $p(|x|)$, then a finite nondeterministic Turing machine decides $L$ with that error bound in polynomial time, halting on every choice string of the prescribed length.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a function from natural numbers to rational numbers
$L$ is a language of bit strings
